Patient information files are created in the hospital system at hsslkq.linkedcare.cn — and only after you receive the treatment plan from the dentist. Photos are only uploaded once the patient has confirmed they're coming to China and sent flight ticket information.

Requesting photos

Message to send after the photo guide

"To provide a more accurate evaluation of your teeth, could you please send us the five photos shown above? This will help our dentist make a careful evaluation and prepare a personalized treatment plan tailored to your dental condition."

Clear, accurate photos let our dentists assess the oral condition and give a more accurate preliminary recommendation. Sequence to remember: greet → understand expectations → request photos → dentist evaluates → quote.

Our public channels: Facebook, Instagram and TikTok pages for Huangshan Dental / Huangshan International Dental Hospital — customers often ask for these to learn more about the company.

What else may be on the implant exam

You asked what to prepare beyond the chapter itself. Based on how the manual is written, these are the areas most likely to appear that aren't obviously "implant" topics.

Anatomy vocabulary

Alveolar bone, periodontal ligament, pulp, dentin, enamel. Implant questions are written using these words — a definition question is cheap for an examiner to set.

Materials cross-questions

"What is a crown made of?" "What is an implant screw made of?" "Do we use titanium for all implant screws?" The manual has an explicit materials quiz that mixes fillings, inlays, crowns and implants together.

Imaging decisions

When to request an X-ray vs a CBCT, and when neither is needed. Directly tied to the implant workflow's preoperative stage.

Numbers & thresholds

Glucose, blood pressure, bone height/width, healing durations, founding years, suture removal days. The single highest-density source of exam marks.

Brand facts & the neutrality rule

Country, founding year, signature technology for all three implant brands — plus "what should you never say to a client."

Sequencing questions

Put the stages in order; what happens within 48 hours; what happens at 6 months. Order-based questions are extremely common with a 3-stage workflow.

Postoperative care

Stage I vs Stage II differences, and the sinus-lift-specific rules (no nose blowing, no diving, no air travel).

Role-play / scripting

"A patient says X — how do you reply?" This is a consultant exam, so expect at least a few. Practice saying them out loud.

If you only have one hour left before the exam

Re-read three things: the numbers table at the top, the contraindications list (with "not an automatic no" attached to each), and the brand grid — material vs surface vs design for Straumann, TiUnite vs SLActive, and 1997 vs 2015.

Part 5

Self-test — 237 questions

Tap a question to reveal its answer, then mark yourself ✓ or ✗. Your running score is in the bar at the top. Questions taken directly from the manual's own quizzes are marked [manual]; the rest are written from manual content to cover angles an examiner is likely to use.

A · Foundations — anatomy, materials, imaging

30 questions
F1Which is the hardest substance in the human body?
A. EnamelB. DentinC. ZirconiaD. Alveolar bone
AEnamel.It cannot grow back once significantly damaged — which is why lost enamel is always a permanent trade-off, including with veneers.
F2A patient feels sensitivity to cold, hot and sweet. Decay has most likely reached which layer?
A. EnamelB. DentinC. PulpD. Root
BDentin.Dentin contains microscopic tubes connected to the nerve. Pulp involvement gives severe throbbing pain and swelling, not just sensitivity.
F3What does the pulp contain?
AnswerNerves, blood vessels and connective tissue.Infection here → severe toothache, throbbing pain, swelling → usually root canal treatment.
F4What is the alveolar bone, and what happens to it in gum disease?
AnswerThe jawbone surrounding the roots, which holds teeth in place. In gum disease this bone gradually disappears.This is the direct cause of the "insufficient bone" contraindication for implants.
F5What is the periodontal ligament (PDL) and what does it do?
AnswerA thin layer of soft tissue connecting the natural tooth to the jawbone. It acts as a cushion, absorbing chewing forces and allowing the tooth to move slightly during biting.An implant has no PDL — it is fused directly to bone.
F6How many teeth does an adult normally have, and how do they break down by type?
Answer32 total: 8 incisors (cutting), 4 canines (tearing), 8 premolars (crushing), 12 molars (grinding).
F7Another name for the third molar is…
A. First bicuspidB. Second bicuspidC. Wisdom toothD. Canine
CWisdom tooth.Also: first premolar = first bicuspid, second premolar = second bicuspid.
F8[manual] In the FDI system, what is tooth 21?
AnswerUpper left central incisor.
F9[manual] What is tooth 48?
AnswerLower right third molar (wisdom tooth).First digit 4 = lower right quadrant; second digit 8 = eighth tooth from the midline.
F10[manual] What is tooth 44?
AnswerLower right first premolar (first bicuspid).
F11[manual] What is tooth 32?
AnswerLower left lateral incisor.
F12A patient asks: "What is a panoramic X-ray?" Give the good consultant answer.
Answer"It's a full-mouth X-ray that shows all of your teeth, jawbone and wisdom teeth in a single image."
F13A patient asks: "Why do I need a CBCT scan?" Give the good consultant answer.
Answer"It's a 3D scan that shows your teeth, bone, nerves and surrounding structures in detail before treatment."
F14Should you routinely ask a patient to get a CBCT before the dentist reviews their case?
NoCT scans are more expensive than standard X-rays and are usually only required for specific treatments — implants, bone grafting, impacted wisdom teeth, complex procedures. In many cases the dentist reviews the X-ray first and then decides.
F15Which treatments usually need NO X-ray or CT at the initial consultation?
AnswerCosmetic treatments: teeth whitening, veneers and minor smile design procedures — provided the patient has no symptoms of gum disease, tooth pain, infection or other significant dental problems.
F16Does fluoride treatment repair a cavity?
NoA common misunderstanding. Fluoride strengthens weakened enamel before a hole forms — it does not fix holes. Applied as gel, foam or varnish.
F17What is the difference between an inlay and an onlay?
AnswerInlay = fits inside the tooth. Onlay = inside the tooth plus covers part of the chewing surface (extends over one or more cusps).
F18Why can a filling be done in one visit but an inlay, onlay or crown cannot?
AnswerInlays, onlays and crowns are custom-made restorations produced in a dental lab, so the patient waits a few days. A simple filling is placed directly in the mouth.
F19How long does a composite filling typically last?
A. 1–3 yearsB. 15–20 yearsC. LifetimeD. 5–10 years
D5–10 years — depending on oral hygiene, diet, teeth grinding and the size of the filling.
F20Does a crown replace the root of the tooth?
NoThe natural root usually remains in place. The crown covers only the visible portion above the gum line. Only an implant replaces the root.
F21Why is a root canal on a back tooth more expensive?
Answer"Back teeth are often more complex because they have multiple roots and canals that require additional treatment."
F22[manual] What material is used for a composite filling?
AnswerResin.
F23[manual] What material is used for an inlay or onlay?
AnswerCeramic or zirconia.
F24[manual] What material is a crown mostly made of?
AnswerMostly zirconia.
F25[manual] What material is an implant screw made of — and do we use titanium for ALL implant screws?
AnswerTitanium — but no, not for all. Straumann implant screws use Roxolid (85% titanium, 15% zirconium).This is the manual's own trick question. The expected answer to "do we use titanium for all implant screws?" is literally "No."
F26Which material is used for veneers because of its high translucency and excellent aesthetics?
A. Lithium disilicate (IPS e.max / glass ceramic)B. ZirconiaC. Composite resinD. Titanium
ALithium disilicate.Its weakness: not as strong as zirconia for heavy back-teeth biting.
F27What is the main disadvantage of zirconia listed in the materials table?
AnswerMore expensive than resin and many ceramics, and it can be less translucent than glass ceramics.
F28Why is titanium not used for visible aesthetic surfaces?
AnswerIt's a metal — strong and biocompatible, ideal inside bone (implants, titanium bases, titanium frameworks), but it does not look like a tooth.
F29A patient asks "Will I be asleep?" — what's the correct consultant answer?
Answer"Local anaesthesia numbs the area. Sedation helps you relax. Depending on the type of sedation, you may be very relaxed but not completely asleep."
F30A patient asks "Will cleaning make my teeth white?"
Answer"Cleaning removes plaque and stains. Whitening changes the colour of the teeth to make them appear whiter."Two different things — never let a patient book a cleaning expecting a whitening result.

B · Implants — multiple choice

40 questions
M1[manual] What does Roxolid refer to?
A. Surface technologyB. MaterialC. DesignD. Implant shape
BMaterial.
M2[manual] What does SLActive refer to?
A. MaterialB. DesignC. SurfaceD. Bone type
CSurface.
M3[manual] What does "tapered" refer to?
A. A materialB. A surface technologyC. I don't knowD. A design
DA design.
M4[manual] What does BLT stand for?
A. Bone Level TaperedB. Bone Level TitaniumC. Basic Long-Term implantD. Bone Lining Technique
ABone Level Tapered.
M5[manual] What is Roxolid?
A. A surface coatingB. A materialC. A design of materialD. I don't know
BA material.
M6[manual] Why was Roxolid developed?
A. To make implants cheaperB. To improve colour of implantsC. To provide higher strengthD. To reduce surgery time only
CTo provide higher strength.
M7[manual] Why was SLActive developed?
A. To increase healing timeB. To change implant shapeC. To replace titaniumD. To reduce healing time and improve bone integration
DTo reduce healing time and improve bone integration.
M8[manual] Why was the tapered implant design developed?
A. To improve stability in boneB. To reduce costC. To make implants smallerD. To avoid surgery
ATo improve stability in bone.
M9[manual] What implant shape was commonly used in the past?
A. TaperedB. CylindricalC. SpiralD. Mixed
BCylindrical.
M10[manual] The origin of Straumann is:
A. USAB. GermanyC. SwitzerlandD. Italy
CSwitzerland — based in Basel.
M11Roxolid is composed of:
A. 100% Grade 4 titaniumB. 85% zirconium + 15% titaniumC. 50/50 titanium and zirconiaD. 85% titanium + 15% zirconium
D85% titanium, 15% zirconium.
M12In which year did Straumann develop Roxolid?
A. 2009B. 1954C. 1997D. 2015
A2009.Careful: 1954 = company founded; 2015 = Straumann's first tapered implant; 1997 = NobelReplace, the world's first tapered implant.
M13The three parts of a dental implant, from bone to mouth, are:
A. Crown → abutment → fixtureB. Fixture → abutment → crownC. Abutment → fixture → crownD. Fixture → crown → abutment
BImplant body (fixture) → abutment → crown.
M14Minimum bone dimensions below which bone is considered insufficient:
A. Height <3 mm, width <5 mmB. Height <10 mm, width <5 mmC. Height <5 mm, width <3 mmD. Height <5 mm, width <5 mm
CHeight < 5 mm, width < 3 mm.Memory hook: height is the bigger number — a tooth is taller than it is wide.
M15Blood pressure limits before implant surgery:
A. Systolic <90, diastolic <140 mmHgB. Systolic <120, diastolic <80 mmHgC. Systolic <160, diastolic <100 mmHgD. Systolic <140, diastolic <90 mmHg
DSystolic under 140 mmHg, diastolic under 90 mmHg.
M16Normal fasting blood glucose is:
A. 3.9–6.1 mmol/LB. ≥7.0 mmol/LC. ≥11.1 mmol/LD. 7.0–11.1 mmol/L
A3.9–6.1 mmol/L.≥7.0 fasting and ≥11.1 post-meal are the diabetes thresholds.
M17The minimum age at which an implant should be placed:
A. 16B. 18–21C. 25D. No minimum
B18–21 years.
M18A delayed implant means the dentist waits approximately how long after extraction?
A. 6 weeksB. 3 monthsC. 6 monthsD. 12 months
C6 months.
M19Which bone procedure is used ONLY in the upper jaw?
A. General bone graftingB. Socket preservationC. PiezosurgeryD. Sinus lift
DSinus lift — used in the upper back teeth area, lifting the sinus membrane and placing graft underneath.
M20Healing time after a bone graft before an implant can be placed:
A. 3–6 monthsB. 2–4 weeksC. 1–2 monthsD. 12 months
A3–6 months — one of the three drawbacks of grafting (extra surgery, long healing, delayed placement).
M21Osseointegration takes approximately:
A. 3–6 weeksB. 3–6 monthsC. 6–12 monthsD. 48 hours
B3–6 months.
M22For a full-mouth case where 16 teeth are removed, how many implants are typically placed?
A. 16B. 10–14C. 4–6D. 8
C4–6 implants; the rest of the arch is a fixed bridge supported by them.
M23A traditional full-arch implant replacement (1 tooth = 1 implant) would need:
A. 4–6 implants per archB. 8 implants per archC. 16 implants per archD. 10–14 implants per arch
D10–14 per arch — very expensive, more surgery time, more bone required, longer healing.
M24Temporary crown or bridge after Stage I surgery is installed within:
A. 48 hoursB. 24 hoursC. 1 weekD. 3 months
A48 hours.
M25Sutures after Stage I implant surgery are removed after:
A. 3–5 daysB. 7–14 daysC. 7–10 daysD. 3 weeks
B7–14 days for Stage I.Stage II is 7–10 days — the shorter one, because Stage II is the milder surgery.
M26After Stage II surgery, how long must the patient avoid alcohol and smoking?
A. Alcohol 2 weeks, smoking 1 weekB. Both 1 weekC. Alcohol 1 week, smoking 2 weeksD. Both 1 month
CNo alcohol for 1 week; no smoking for 2 weeks, then no more than 3 cigarettes per day.
M27Which is NOT one of the three preoperative physical checks?
A. Blood pressure measurementB. Blood glucose measurementC. Blood function test (AP/TTP)D. Cholesterol measurement
DCholesterol is not part of the three-step preoperative examination.
M28Which is NOT one of the six sub-steps of "formulate a personalized plan"?
A. Shade selectionB. Economic considerationC. Implant brand selectionD. Auxiliary surgical judgment
AShade selection belongs to the veneer/crown workflow, not the implant planning stage.The six are: oral condition assessment · patient needs confirmation · economic consideration · implant brand selection · quantity and position determination · auxiliary surgical judgment.
M29Nobel Biocare's country of origin and founding year:
A. Switzerland, 1954B. Sweden, 1981C. Germany, 1924D. South Korea, 2002
BSweden, 1981. Parent company: Envista (USA).
M30Which company introduced the All-on-4® treatment concept, and in which year?
A. Straumann, 2009B. MegaGen, 2002C. Nobel Biocare, 1998D. Ivoclar, 2005
CNobel Biocare, 1998.
M31What does "CC" in NobelReplace CC stand for?
A. Ceramic CoatingB. Compromised CasesC. Cylindrical CoreD. Conical Connection
DConical Connection.
M32Which surface technology belongs to Nobel Biocare?
A. TiUniteB. SLActiveC. RoxolidD. BLT
ATiUnite — an anodized titanium surface. SLActive is Straumann's.
M33Platform shifting means:
A. The implant is placed at an angleB. The abutment is slightly smaller than the implant platformC. The crown is offset from the implantD. The implant platform sits above the gum
BThe abutment is slightly smaller than the implant platform, creating extra space for the gums to grow — healthier soft tissue and a more natural-looking smile.
M34Which is NOT a listed benefit of a conical connection?
A. Tight seal reducing bacterial leakageB. Improved connection stabilityC. Faster osseointegrationD. Reduced micro-movement
CFaster osseointegration is a surface benefit (SLActive/TiUnite), not a connection benefit.
M35NobelActive's signature thread feature is:
A. Platform shiftingB. Conical connectionC. Hydrophilic surfaceD. Double-lead thread
DDouble-lead thread — plus sharp cutting blades.
M36MegaGen's origin and founding year:
A. South Korea, 2002B. Japan, 1995C. China, 2001D. South Korea, 1981
ASouth Korea, 2002.Don't confuse with Upcera — China, 2001, from the Tsinghua University Ceramic Laboratory.
M37Which crown material is used on a titanium base?
A. ZirconiaB. Resin (PMMA-based photopolymer)C. PorcelainD. Lithium disilicate
BResin. Zirconia is used on a titanium framework.
M38A titanium framework is made by:
A. Casting molten titaniumB. 3D printingC. Milling a titanium disc (blank) with CAD/CAMD. Buying it from the implant manufacturer
CMilled from a titanium disc (titanium blank) by a CAD/CAM machine — a custom-made restoration, not purchased from the manufacturer.
M39Which patients receive immediate temporary teeth?
A. Single implant patientsB. Two-implant patientsC. All implant patientsD. All-on-4 / All-on-6 patients (full or half arch)
DOnly All-on-4/6 patients. Patients with one or two implants "go back toothless."
M40Which of these is an ABSOLUTE reason a patient can never have an implant?
A. Controlled hypertensionB. BruxismC. Insufficient boneD. None of the above are automatic disqualifications
DNone of them. Controlled hypertension is fine after evaluation; bruxism is managed with a night guard; insufficient bone is solved with a graft or sinus lift.This is the single most important conceptual point in the whole implant chapter.

C · Implants — true or false

25 questions
T1[manual] Straumann uses the TiUnite surface.
FalseStraumann uses SLActive. TiUnite is Nobel Biocare's.
T2[manual] NobelReplace CC comes with the TiUnite surface.
True
T3[manual] NobelReplace CC comes with a double-lead thread.
FalseDouble-lead thread is a NobelActive feature.
T4[manual] NobelActive comes with a double-lead thread.
True
T5[manual] NobelActive comes with sharp cutting blades.
True
T6[manual] Both NobelReplace CC and Straumann BLT have a tapered design.
True
T7[manual] I should tell the client that, based on scientific evidence, NobelReplace CC provides better stability than Straumann BLT.
FalseNever rank one brand above another to a client. Both are world-leading with excellent long-term clinical success; the dentist decides based on the individual case.
T8[manual] Both NobelReplace CC and NobelActive have a long clinical record.
True~20 years and ~15 years respectively.
T9[manual] I should tell the client to purchase NobelActive.
FalseNever push a specific product. Present facts and let the dentist and patient decide.
T10[manual] I should always recommend NobelReplace CC because it is cheaper than NobelActive.
FalseRecommendations follow the patient's bone condition and treatment plan, not price alone.
T11[manual] Sometimes dentists have difficulty placing implants into the patient's mouth due to insufficient bone.
TrueExactly the scenario NobelActive and Roxolid are marketed to address.
T12[manual] NobelReplace CC and NobelActive are from the same company.
TrueBoth are Nobel Biocare systems.
T13[manual] Nobel Biocare is a brand from Sweden.
TrueFounded 1981; parent company Envista (USA).
T14Roxolid is available from several implant manufacturers.
FalseRoxolid is proprietary to Straumann — developed by them and not a generic material used by all manufacturers.
T15Straumann does not have a conical connection.
FalseStraumann implants do have a conical connection — the manual states this explicitly.
T16Straumann does not have platform switching.
FalseStraumann does have platform switching — it just isn't always labelled the same way in marketing.
T17Because Nobel has 25+ years of tapered-implant data and Straumann does not, Straumann's implant is inferior.
FalseThe manual answers this directly: "No. Straumann has also conducted many clinical studies and has achieved excellent clinical success." It simply doesn't have 25+ years of data specifically for tapered design.
T18A patient with well-controlled hypertension can usually receive an implant.
TrueMany patients with controlled hypertension safely undergo implant treatment after evaluation by the dentist or oral surgeon.
T19Bruxism disqualifies a patient from getting implants.
FalseThe dentist will recommend a custom night guard to protect the implants during sleep.
T20A patient who lacks adequate jawbone density is automatically disqualified from implants.
False"If you lack adequate jawbone density, you're not automatically disqualified." Solutions: bone graft or sinus lift.
T21A fixed bridge can develop cavities like a natural tooth.
FalseIt is artificial so it doesn't get cavities — but it can wear down over time depending on material (resin faster, zirconia slower), and hygiene is still needed to keep gums and implants healthy.
T22The Stage II postoperative reaction is generally milder than Stage I.
TrueSimple Stage II cases usually need no anti-inflammatory or detumescent medication at all.
T23A healing cap falling off before the final prosthesis is fitted is an emergency.
FalseIt's a normal phenomenon — but the patient should contact the doctor as soon as possible to reposition it.
T24After a sinus lift, the patient may fly frequently as long as they feel well.
FalseWithin 1 month they must avoid diving, frequent air travel and high-pressure environments.
T25A customer can order a titanium base with a zirconia crown.
False"No. It is not possible for us to manufacture it."

D · Implants — short answer & recall

30 questions
S1Name the three parts of a dental implant and what each does.
Answer1. Implant body (fixture) — titanium screw in the jawbone, acts as the artificial root. 2. Abutment — connects the implant to the crown. 3. Crown — the visible tooth, made from zirconia or composite resin.
S2Why is an implant different from a filling, inlay or crown?
AnswerAn implant replaces both the root and the visible part of the tooth. The others only restore the part above the gum.
S3List all seven implant indications.
Answer1. Missing one tooth · 2. Missing multiple teeth · 3. Missing all teeth · 4. Tooth cannot be saved · 5. Patient wants a fixed solution · 6. Loose or unstable denture · 7. Patient wants better chewing function.
S4Give three reasons a single missing tooth is a good implant indication.
AnswerIt replaces the missing root · it replaces the missing tooth · it doesn't require shaving down the neighbouring teeth.
S5Under "tooth cannot be saved," what three conditions are listed?
AnswerSevere decay · vertical fracture · failed root canal.
S6List all nine implant contraindications.
Answer1. Uncontrolled diabetes · 2. Active gum disease (periodontitis) · 3. Severe smoking · 4. Insufficient bone · 5. Poor oral hygiene · 6. Serious medical conditions · 7. Bruxism · 8. Blood pressure / age under 18–21 · 9. Pregnancy.
S7What three effects does high blood sugar have on implant treatment?
AnswerSlows healing · higher infection risk · higher implant failure risk.
S8Name the "serious medical conditions" listed as contraindications.
AnswerRecent heart attack or severe heart failure · uncontrolled hypertension · immune disorders (e.g. active lupus/SLE) · serious bleeding/coagulation disorders such as haemophilia · advanced cancer · advanced AIDS · severe psychiatric / mental disorders.
S9What is haemophilia, and what three surgical problems does it cause?
AnswerA genetic disease where the blood does not clot normally. The patient may bleed for a long time after surgery, may bleed excessively after a tooth extraction, and has increased surgical risks.
S10What are the signs a patient may have bruxism?
AnswerJaw pain, headaches, worn-down teeth. Many people grind at night without realizing it.
S11Name six situations where a patient may choose a bridge instead of an implant.
AnswerNot enough bone and doesn't want grafting · medical condition makes surgery risky · wants faster treatment · wants a lower-cost option · uncomfortable with surgery · the adjacent teeth already need crowns.
S12What is the main drawback of a dental bridge?
AnswerThe dentist must file down healthy teeth to attach the crowns, which changes them permanently.
S13Explain "bone preservation" as a benefit of implants — including the facial-structure point.
AnswerImplants transmit chewing forces to the jawbone, which helps maintain a healthy jaw and preserve facial structure. If a tooth is missing, the bone around it receives no stimulation and slowly recedes — and with shrinking bone, the shape of the face may also change over time.
S14Give four reasons a dentist would choose a delayed implant.
AnswerInfection was present around the tooth · bone needs time to heal · bone grafting is needed · the extraction site is not suitable for immediate implant placement.
S15What are the three problems with bone grafting?
AnswerIt requires additional surgery · healing time is long (usually 3 to 6 months) · it delays implant placement.
S16What happens if an implant is placed without sufficient bone and without grafting?
AnswerThe implant may not achieve proper stability, because an implant has a fixed diameter and requires sufficient surrounding bone.
S17How can an implant be achieved without a bone graft?
AnswerBecause Roxolid is stronger, dentists can use smaller-diameter implants while still maintaining the strength needed to withstand normal biting and chewing forces.
S18Describe, in 7 steps, how a tapered implant creates primary stability.
Answer1. The narrow tip enters the hole easily. 2. As it goes deeper the diameter gradually increases. 3. The wider part pushes against the surrounding bone. 4. This slightly compresses the bone. 5. Bone is elastic, so the compressed bone pushes back like a spring. 6. The implant threads also grip the bone. 7. Bone compression + thread engagement = a strong mechanical lock called primary stability.
S19Are most bolts used in everyday life tapered? Why does the answer matter?
AnswerNo — most everyday bolts are cylindrical (straight-sided), with the diameter staying almost the same the whole length. The dental implant is deliberately different because the taper is what produces primary stability, especially in soft bone.
S20Define osseointegration in the manual's own words.
Answer"It means the bone grows tightly around the implant and locks it in place like a natural tooth root."
S21Explain the four-step mechanism by which SLActive speeds up healing.
AnswerIt is highly hydrophilic (water-attracting), so: blood spreads quickly over the implant surface → a clot and early healing layer form immediately → this healing layer creates a "friendly surface" → bone cells start attaching and building new bone.
S22Explain how TiUnite works, and how it differs from SLActive.
AnswerTiUnite is an anodized titanium surface that increases the roughness of the implant, with tiny grooves that let bone cells attach more easily and grow stronger. SLActive is a hydrophilic surface that attracts blood and biological fluids immediately to accelerate early healing. Both improve osseointegration — different mechanisms: roughness vs wettability.
S23Give Straumann's founding year, city, country and global reach.
AnswerFounded 1954, based in Basel, Switzerland. Operating in 100+ countries; one of the world's top premium dental implant companies.
S24List the six NobelReplace CC marketing keywords.
AnswerProven performance · enhanced aesthetics · tapered design · conical connection · platform shifting · natural-looking aesthetics.
S25List the five NobelActive keywords.
AnswerDouble-lead threads · sharp cutting blades · stability · aesthetics · long clinical record (15 years).
S26What is the difference between NobelReplace CC and NobelActive?
AnswerBoth are Nobel Biocare systems with the same goal — replacing missing teeth. The difference is design and the situations they're used in: NobelReplace CC for normal or moderately challenging bone; NobelActive for more challenging situations where higher primary stability is required.The manual flags this answer as "for your own understanding" — avoid sending it directly to a client.
S27Give the three-line chain showing where a titanium base sits.
AnswerCrown → Titanium Base / Titanium Framework → Implant. Both are types of abutment ("titanium abutment").
S28State the three differences between a titanium base and a titanium framework.
Answer1. The framework is stronger and more expensive. 2. The base is used for temporary or individual implant restorations; the framework for full-arch final restorations. 3. The base is used during the early healing phase after surgery; the framework after the patient returns (around 6 months) for the final prosthesis.
S29Why use a resin crown on a titanium base instead of zirconia?
AnswerResin absorbs chewing forces, is easy to adjust and is safer during the healing phase. Zirconia is much more rigid and does not absorb force, so it transfers higher stress to the implant during the early healing period.
S30Why is resin NOT used on a titanium framework?
AnswerResin is not strong enough for long-term final restorations and wears down over time — so zirconia is used instead.

E · Implants — client scenarios (say it out loud)

15 questions
C1"I have diabetes. Can I get implants?"
Say"Many diabetic patients successfully receive implants. The dentist will review your blood sugar control and medical history to determine whether implant treatment is appropriate."Note what you did NOT do: quote numbers, or say no.
C2"I have hypertension — I suppose that rules me out?"
Say"Not at all. Blood pressure just needs to be well controlled before surgery. Many patients with controlled hypertension safely undergo implant treatment after evaluation by the dentist or oral surgeon."
C3"I grind my teeth badly at night."
Say"Bruxism doesn't disqualify you from getting implants. The dentist will recommend wearing a custom night guard to protect your implants while you sleep."
C4"Are there any risks when placing dental implants?"
Say"Today implant therapy is an established standard for tooth replacement, and it's well documented that implants are an extremely safe and successful method. Potential risks can vary depending on your health, so your dentist will do a thorough assessment to confirm implant treatment is the right choice for you."
C5"Which is better, Straumann or Nobel?"
Say"Both Straumann and Nobel Biocare are world-leading implant brands with excellent long-term clinical success. The difference lies in the materials used, design structure and surface technology, which influence osseointegration and long-term stability. The best choice depends on your bone condition, aesthetic needs and treatment plan — our dentist will carefully evaluate your case and recommend the most suitable system."Never say "Nobel is better" or "Straumann is better."
C6"What's the difference between Straumann BLT and NobelReplace CC?"
Say"Both feature a tapered implant design that provides excellent stability. NobelReplace CC features the TiUnite surface, designed for strong long-term bone stability; Straumann BLT features SLActive, designed to promote faster healing. The best choice depends on your bone condition, aesthetic needs and treatment plan — our dentist will evaluate your case."
C7"You're removing 16 of my teeth — will I get 16 implants?"
Say"No. Only 4–6 implants are placed in the jawbone. The other teeth are not implants — they're attached as a fixed bridge supported by those implants."
C8"Why not do one implant per tooth? Isn't that stronger?"
Say"A traditional full-mouth replacement needs 10–14 implants per arch — very expensive, more surgery time, more bone required and a longer healing time. All-on-4 or All-on-6 supports a full arch with fewer implants, reducing cost and treatment time."
C9"What's the difference between All-on-4 and All-on-6?"
Say"All-on-6 has more implants, so it provides better support, stronger bite force distribution and more long-term stability. All-on-4 uses fewer implants, so it's usually more suitable for patients with bone loss and is more cost-effective."
C10"Will I have teeth when I walk out of the hospital?" — a single-implant patient.
AnswerFor one or two implants there is usually no immediate loading — the patient goes back without a temporary tooth in that space, and returns after 4–6 months for the abutment and final crown. Only All-on-4/6 patients get same-day temporary teeth.Say it kindly, but say it clearly — this is exactly the expectation gap that creates complaints.
C11"Why do I need to come back after 4–6 months?"
Say"To allow osseointegration — the implant healing into the bone — before the final teeth are placed."
C12"What is Roxolid?" — client shows mild curiosity but isn't technical.
Say (basic)"Roxolid® is a titanium–zirconium alloy developed by Straumann. It's stronger than standard titanium and provides excellent stability in bone, even in difficult clinical conditions, helping improve long-term implant success."Only give the 85/15 composition and the bone-graft-avoidance detail if they ask for more.
C13"What is SLActive?"
Say (basic)"A cutting-edge implant surface technology that quickly activates the body's natural healing process immediately after placement. This leads to faster healing, stronger bone integration and improved long-term implant success."
C14You want to introduce NobelActive. What should you avoid saying, and why?
AnswerAvoid "upgraded version of NobelReplace CC" — customers hear it as pure marketing. Avoid technical terms like "tapered design" and "double-lead thread" — use "smart design" instead. Always give country of origin (Sweden) and always quote the price.
C15A client asks a detailed technical question about implant metallurgy. What's the manual's guidance?
AnswerDo not send the detailed answer unless the client wants to know more. Avoid technical descriptions unless the client is interested. Also: don't rely on AI for product claims — use official keywords so you never exaggerate a benefit, because deep product knowledge is what builds client trust.

F · Veneers — multiple choice

28 questions
V1A veneer is best defined as:
A. A thin shell attached to the front of a natural toothB. A cap covering the whole toothC. A replacement for a missing tooth including its rootD. A filling material
AA thin porcelain or composite shell attached to the front of a natural tooth to improve its appearance.
V2Which is an ABSOLUTE contraindication for veneers?
A. Severe bruxismB. Very little enamel remainingC. Large existing fillingsD. Very young patient
BVery little enamel remaining.The other three are relative contraindications.
V3Which is a RELATIVE contraindication for veneers?
A. Active gum diseaseB. Large cavities / active decayC. Receding gums (depending on severity)D. Severely crooked teeth
CReceding gums.A, B and C are the absolute ones — along with very little enamel remaining.
V4Mild fluorosis is listed as:
A. An absolute contraindicationB. A relative contraindicationC. Not mentionedD. An indication
DAn indication — mild fluorosis is one of the eight reasons veneers are appropriate.
V5Approximately how much enamel is removed for a porcelain veneer?
A. 0.5 mmB. 0.1 mmC. 1.5 mmD. None
AAbout 0.5 mm.
V6Veneers need to be replaced after approximately:
A. 2–5 yearsB. 10–15 yearsC. 25–30 yearsD. Never
B10 to 15 years, per the disadvantages list.Individual brand durability differs: Upcera 6–10 yrs, e.max and VITA 15–25 yrs.
V7Which step comes immediately after the acid etching gel when placing a veneer?
A. Resin cementB. Curing lightC. Bonding agentD. Impression
CBonding agent — it acts like a primer. Then resin cement + curing light.
V8Why is acid etching gel applied to the tooth?
A. To whiten the toothB. To numb the toothC. To disinfect the toothD. To create microscopic roughness so cement adheres strongly
DTo create microscopic roughness on the tooth surface so the cement can adhere strongly.
V9On which floor is intraoral scanning performed?
A. 3rd floorB. 1st floorC. 4th floorD. Basement
A3rd floor. CAD, CAM, milling, furnaces, polishing and glazing are all on the 4th floor.
V10Which CAM software is used in our lab?
A. AutoCADB. WorkNCC. exocadD. SolidWorks
BWorkNC — it converts the CAD design into step-by-step machine instructions and plans how the veneer will be cut, then transfers data to the milling machine over the network.
V11Milling a single veneer takes approximately:
A. 2–5 minutesB. 1.5 hoursC. 10–20 minutesD. 11 hours
C10–20 minutes.Crown milling is 15–20 minutes; 1.5 hours is veneer crystallization; 11 hours is crown sintering.
V12How long does veneer crystallization take?
A. 20 minutesB. 6 hoursC. 11 hoursD. ~1.5 hours per firing
DApproximately 1.5 hours per firing — and that's for the entire furnace cycle, which can hold multiple veneers at once, not per veneer.
V13Straight after milling, a veneer looks:
A. White, chalky or slightly bluish, soft and roughB. Glossy and final-colouredC. Grey and metallicD. Transparent
AWhite, chalky or slightly bluish; soft; rough surface; no shine; no final colour depth — though the shape is already accurate.
V14Which process gives the veneer its final strength, shade and translucency?
A. MillingB. CrystallizationC. GlazingD. Polishing
BCrystallization in the ceramic furnace.
V15What is "layering"?
A. Stacking multiple veneersB. Applying glazeC. Hand-applying a ceramic (porcelain powder) layer over the crystallized restorationD. Cementing the veneer in layers
CA technician hand-applies ceramic powder over the crystallized restoration to improve translucency, enhance colour, create natural detail and make it look more like a real tooth. Then it's fired again.
V16Ivoclar's veneering (layering) material is called:
A. IPS e.max CADB. VITA AmberC. ZenostarD. IPS e.max Ceram
DIPS e.max Ceram.CAD = the block that gets milled (shape and strength). Ceram = the hand-layered powder (beauty and natural appearance).
V17Glazing improves which three things?
A. Surface smoothness, natural gloss, stain resistanceB. Strength, fit, shadeC. Translucency, opacity, colourD. Bonding, adhesion, durability
ASurface smoothness, natural gloss and stain resistance.The manual's analogy: like adding varnish to a wooden table.
V18A CAD block for a glass ceramic veneer is usually made of:
A. ZirconiaB. Lithium disilicateC. TitaniumD. Composite resin
BLithium disilicate or another advanced glass ceramic material.
V19Upcera originated from which institution and in which year?
A. Peking University Ceramic Lab, 2001B. ETH Zurich, 1923C. Tsinghua University Ceramic Laboratory, 2001D. Tsinghua University, 2010
CThe Tsinghua University Ceramic Laboratory in China, 2001.
V20Ivoclar was founded in:
A. 1924, GermanyB. 1954, BaselC. 2005, LiechtensteinD. 1923, Zurich, Switzerland
DFounded 1923 in Zurich, Switzerland; headquarters now in Schaan, Liechtenstein. Operates in 130+ countries with 3,700+ employees.1924 = VITA Zahnfabrik (Germany). 2005 = IPS e.max launch.
V21IPS e.max lithium disilicate glass-ceramic was introduced in:
A. 2005B. 1998C. 2001D. 2010
A2005 — and it quickly became the benchmark for all dental glass-ceramics.
V22IPS e.max's clinical survival rate is approximately:
A. 75%B. 95%C. 85%D. 99.9%
BApproximately 95%.
V23VITA Amber's material is:
A. Lithium disilicateB. Pure zirconiaC. Zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate (ZLS) glass ceramicD. Feldspathic porcelain
CZirconia-reinforced lithium silicate (ZLS) glass ceramic.This is the one material name that differs from the other two brands — a likely exam target.
V24Which translucency level is used when the underlying tooth is dark or yellow?
A. HTB. MTC. Any of themD. LT
DLT — Low Translucency. It blocks the underlying colour and improves the final appearance.HT is used when the natural tooth is already light or white.
V25Which level is used to mask moderately discoloured teeth or metal posts?
A. MOB. HTC. MTD. LT
AMO — Medium Opacity. It blocks the most light.
V26Which is the brightest bleach shade?
A. BL2B. BL1C. BL3D. BL4
BBL1 — the whitest, commonly selected for smile makeover cases. BL4 is the darkest of the bleach shades.
V27Do we perform composite veneers at our hospital?
A. Yes, in one visitB. Yes, but only for front teethC. NoD. Only for children
CNo — we do not do composite veneers.But never end the conversation there. Redirect to ultra-thin porcelain veneers.
V28How many visits does a veneer case usually take?
A. 2B. 3C. Depends on the brandD. 1
DOne visit — tooth preparation plus veneer placement, no temporary teeth needed, normal function afterwards (avoiding hard food).

G · Veneers — true or false

15 questions
VT1A veneer replaces a missing tooth.
FalseA veneer only re-faces an existing natural tooth. An implant replaces a missing tooth.
VT2Veneers are reversible.
FalseMany types of veneer are not reversible, and at least some natural enamel (~0.5 mm) is permanently lost.
VT3All veneers require layering.
FalseNot all veneers require layering — many cases are completed with only the milled and crystallized restoration. Layering is for the highest-aesthetic cases.
VT4The same intraoral scanner is used for both veneers and crowns.
TrueExplicitly noted in the manual.
VT5Fluoride pitting is a type of tooth decay.
FalseIt is a developmental enamel defect — not tooth decay and not an infection. The teeth can be perfectly healthy but look mottled, pitted, yellowish, brownish or rough.
VT6"E-max" and "IPS e.max" are two different products.
FalseE-MAX is just a shortened name for IPS e.max. Clinics often say "porcelain veneer" when they actually mean IPS e.max glass-ceramic.
VT7An IPS e.max Semi-Handcrafted veneer uses a better ceramic material than a standard e.max veneer.
FalseBoth use the same premium IPS e.max material. The difference is extra artistic work — hand-applied IPS e.max Ceram — for a more natural, customized appearance.
VT8Top-Tier and Custom Luxury Handmade veneers use a different ceramic material.
FalseWhat changes: who makes it (senior/master technician), time spent on customization, level of detailing, amount of patient communication. What doesn't necessarily change: the ceramic material, the basic workflow, the layering process itself.
VT9Whitening toothpaste is recommended for maintaining veneers.
FalseDo not use abrasive toothpaste or whitening products — they may scratch or discolour veneers. Use non-abrasive fluoride toothpaste and a soft-bristled brush.
VT10If a veneer comes off, the patient should throw it away and book a new one.
FalseKeep it and contact the dentist immediately for re-bonding.
VT11A patient with severe bruxism can never have veneers.
FalseSevere bruxism is a relative contraindication, not absolute — and a night guard is recommended after placement to prevent chipping and cracking.
VT12Veneer patients should have a dental checkup every 6–12 months.
TrueAnd they should not skip cleanings — the dentist inspects veneer edges and bonding.
VT13Veneers can make teeth more sensitive to heat and cold.
TrueListed among the disadvantages, along with sore gums for a couple of days (ibuprofen helps).
VT14The milling machine used for veneers is located in the laboratory room on the 4th floor.
TrueVeneer milling machine: laboratory room, 4th floor. Crown milling machine (XTCERA): cutting room, 4th floor. CAM computer: cutting room, 4th floor.
VT15We use authentic ceramic blocks sourced directly from manufacturers.
TrueOne of the selling points for "why choose our hospital" — along with experienced doctors and technicians at every stage, a state-of-the-art milling system, advanced layering, photo transparency, and an offer of a video consultation with a virtual tour.

H · Veneers — short answer & recall

22 questions
VS1List the five reasons people get veneers.
AnswerWhiter teeth · closing small gaps · more even-looking teeth · achieving a "Hollywood smile" makeover · fixing chipped edges.
VS2List all eight veneer indications.
AnswerHealthy teeth · healthy gums · discoloured teeth · chipped teeth · small gaps · minor alignment issues · wants smile improvement · mild fluorosis.
VS3List all four ABSOLUTE contraindications for veneers.
AnswerActive gum disease (periodontitis) · large cavities / active decay · very little enamel remaining · severely crooked teeth.
VS4List all eight RELATIVE contraindications for veneers.
AnswerSevere bruxism · malocclusion (deep bite, edge-to-edge bite — may need orthodontics first) · large existing fillings · moderate tooth misalignment · high caries risk · very young patients · receding gums (depending on severity) · poor oral hygiene.
VS5Name the 10 veneer production steps in order.
Answer1. Intraoral scanning (3rd floor) · 1b. Shade selection · 2. CAD design · 3. CAM processing (WorkNC) · 4. Milling · 5. Crystallization (furnace) · 6. Layering (optional) · 7. Glazing · 8. Cleaning and polishing · 9. Quality control · 10. Delivery to clinic.
VS6What three things does the dentist evaluate during shade selection?
AnswerThe patient's natural tooth colour · the patient's aesthetic expectations · whether the patient prefers a natural or brighter smile. The chosen shade is then communicated to the lab on the 4th floor.
VS7What is a CAD block?
AnswerA pre-manufactured block of dental material used in the milling machine — the starting material for a veneer. For glass ceramic veneers it's usually lithium disilicate or another advanced glass ceramic.
VS8Name the three CAD block brands used in our company and their countries.
AnswerUpcera Glass Ceramic — China · IPS e.max CAD (Ivoclar) — Switzerland · VITA Glass Ceramic — Germany.
VS9What four improvements does layering give?
AnswerImproves translucency · enhances colour and shade · creates natural-looking details · makes the restoration look more like a real tooth.
VS10What three checks are performed in veneer quality control?
AnswerSurface cleaning · shade verification · fit and margin check.
VS11Give the six steps of placing a veneer on a tooth.
Answer1. Digital scan or impression · 2. Lab makes the porcelain veneer · 3. Dentist buffs/reshapes the enamel · 4. Acid etching gel for microscopic roughness · 5. Bonding agent (primer) · 6. Veneer attached with resin cement and a curing light.
VS12What are the two types of veneer, and how is each made?
AnswerPorcelain veneers — custom-made in a dental lab from impressions or digital scans, bonded at a later visit. Composite resin veneers — made directly by the dentist in the office: tooth-coloured resin applied, shaped by hand, hardened with a curing light. We only do porcelain.
VS13List the five disadvantages of porcelain veneers.
Answer1. Loss of at least some natural enamel (0.5 mm) · 2. Many types are not reversible · 3. Teeth may become more sensitive to heat and cold · 4. Gums will probably be sore for a couple of days (ibuprofen helps) · 5. Need replacement after 10–15 years.
VS14What three things do veneer patients usually care about?
Answer1. How natural will it look? 2. How long will it last? 3. Why is one veneer 1,680 RMB and another 9,999 RMB?
VS15Give the price and durability for Upcera, VITA Amber and IPS e.max Semi-Handcrafted.
AnswerUpcera 1,680 RMB / 6–10 years · VITA Amber 3,880 RMB / 15–25 years · IPS e.max Semi-Handcrafted 5,880 RMB / 15–25 years (e.max generally 15+ years).
VS16Give the country of origin and material for all three veneer brands.
AnswerUpcera — China, lithium disilicate / advanced glass ceramic. Ivoclar IPS e.max — Switzerland, lithium disilicate glass ceramic. VITA — Germany, zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate (ZLS) glass ceramic.
VS17Why do patients choose IPS e.max? Give three reasons.
AnswerNatural-looking aesthetics and natural translucency (light passes through it) · high strength · proven long-term reliability and durability, with clinical studies showing ~95% survival.
VS18Why do patients choose VITA Amber? Give five reasons.
AnswerPremium German engineering and quality · excellent translucency and lifelike appearance · reliable strength and durability · precise shade matching · natural-looking smile results.
VS19Explain the difference between IPS e.max CAD and IPS e.max Ceram in one sentence.
Answer"IPS e.max CAD provides the shape and strength, while IPS e.max Ceram provides the beauty and natural appearance."
VS20Describe all four translucency levels and when each is used.
AnswerHT — most light through, mimics natural enamel; used when the tooth is already light/white; best for veneers. MT — for cases needing more brightness than HT and more translucency than LT. LT — less light through, balances aesthetics and masking; used when the tooth is dark or yellow; common for crowns and veneers. MO — blocks more light; masks moderately discoloured teeth or metal posts.
VS21List the five categories of post-veneer precautions.
Answer1. Oral hygiene · 2. Diet and eating habits · 3. Protect against damage · 4. Regular dental care · 5. General tips.
VS22Which foods and drinks should veneer patients limit, and what trick reduces the risk?
AnswerStaining foods and drinks — coffee, tea, red wine, cola, curry, soy sauce. Use a straw and rinse the mouth afterwards. Also avoid hard foods (bones, nutshells, hard candy, ice, biting into apples/carrots) and tough/chewy foods (beef jerky, tough meat, sticky candy).

I · Veneers — client scenarios

10 questions
VC1"I want no-prep veneers — I don't want my teeth shaved."
SayDon't just say "we don't offer composite veneers." Explain that composite veneers are generally less durable and don't provide the same level of aesthetics as porcelain. Then introduce our ultra-thin porcelain veneers, which need only around 0.5 mm of preparation — minimally invasive, almost painless, with a more natural and longer-lasting result.The goal is to keep the conversation going, educate the client, and guide them toward porcelain.
VC2"Which is better for me — IPS e.max, VITA or Upcera?"
Say"The main differences are composition, aesthetics, manufacturing process and price. They're all high-quality materials, but each has different advantages for different clinical situations and preferences. The most important factor is choosing the material that best matches your bite condition, smile design and expectations. Once you send us a few photos of your teeth, our dentist can evaluate your case and recommend the most suitable option — including the reasons behind the recommendation."
VC3"Do you offer zirconia veneers?"
Say"If you're specifically looking for zirconia restorations rather than ceramic veneers, we can also offer options such as VITA, a German brand known for excellent quality, especially where greater strength is required. The most important factor is selecting the material that best suits your bite, smile design and expectations — send us a few photos and our dentist can recommend the most appropriate option and explain why."
VC4"Why is one veneer 1,680 and another 9,999?"
AnswerExplain the two axes: material tier (Upcera entry-level glass ceramic 6–10 years vs premium e.max/VITA 15–25 years) and craftsmanship tier (fully milled vs semi-handcrafted with hand layering vs top-tier work by a master technician). Be honest that at the top tier the ceramic and workflow may be the same — what changes is who makes it, how much time is spent, and the level of detailing and personalization.
VC5"What exactly do I get for the Semi-Handcrafted veneer?"
Say"This combines the premium IPS e.max material with additional artistic customization by our dental technicians — meaning more customization and more attention to detail. The veneer is first milled from an IPS e.max CAD block to create the basic shape, then the technician applies IPS e.max Ceram by hand to enhance the aesthetics."
VC6"Why should I come to your hospital for veneers?"
SayExperienced doctors and technicians involved in every stage of fabrication · authentic ceramic blocks sourced directly from manufacturers · a state-of-the-art milling system · advanced layering by skilled technicians for premium aesthetics · photos attached for transparency · and an offer of a video consultation with a personal virtual tour of the hospital and factory.
VC7A patient with visible white streaks and cloudy patches asks what's wrong with their teeth.
AnswerLikely mild fluorosis — a developmental enamel defect from too much fluoride while the teeth were forming in childhood. Reassure: it is not decay and not an infection, and the teeth can be perfectly healthy. If significant, options are veneers, crowns, or whitening if the discolouration is mild.
VC8A patient wants veneers but has bleeding gums and an untreated cavity. What do you do?
AnswerBoth are absolute contraindications — active gum disease and active decay. Don't quote a veneer plan yet. Explain that the dentist will need to treat the gum condition and the decay first, then assess whether veneers are suitable. Request photos and imaging so the dentist can evaluate.
VC9A patient with a deep bite wants a full set of veneers.
AnswerMalocclusion — deep bite or edge-to-edge bite — is a relative contraindication; orthodontic treatment may be needed first. Present it as sequencing, not refusal, and let the dentist assess after photos.
VC10"Will I need an X-ray before veneers?"
AnswerUsually not at the initial consultation — cosmetic treatments such as whitening, veneers and minor smile design don't routinely require imaging, provided the patient has no symptoms of gum disease, tooth pain, infection or other significant dental problems. Photos are still required.

J · Mixed — crowns, timing & consultant workflow

22 questions
X1How long is a zirconia crown sintered, and how does that compare with a veneer's firing?
AnswerCrown sintering ≈ 11 hours. Veneer crystallization ≈ 1.5 hours.Easy to mix up — remember the harder material takes the longer bake.
X2What is a zirconia crown milled from?
AnswerA zirconia disc (or solid block) placed inside the milling machine. Milling takes about 15–20 minutes per crown.
X3What is articulating paper used for?
AnswerIt shows where the bite is too high or where teeth are touching too strongly — used to identify high contact points during occlusion (bite) adjustment. Any areas that are too high are removed little by little until the bite is balanced.
X4When is a crown needed?
AnswerWhen a tooth is heavily decayed · cracked · severely worn down · or after root canal treatment.
X5Give the price, origin and durability of the two crown brands.
AnswerUpcera Zirconia — 1,100 RMB, China, 10+ years. Wieland Zenostar — 1,999 RMB, Germany (later purchased by Ivoclar), 15+ years.
X6What is the difference between "Wieland" and "Zenostar"?
AnswerWieland is the brand; Zenostar is the product line, introduced in 2010. Wieland was founded in 1871 in Germany and is now part of the Ivoclar Vivadent group.
X7A client says "Upcera is cheap, is it any good?" — how do you answer?
Say"The company has a global presence in more than 110 countries and regions, with subsidiaries in Germany, the USA and Colombia. Its zirconia is manufactured under strict quality standards and is designed to meet high clinical expectations, providing reliable aesthetic and functional performance."
X8Which treatments take 1 visit and which take 2? Give the rule.
Answer1 visit: veneers, zirconia crowns. 2 visits: full-mouth implant, half-arch implant, single implant, multiple individual implants, extraction with bridge. Rule: anything requiring bone healing needs a second visit.
X9After an extraction with a bridge, when does the patient return — and do they get same-day teeth?
AnswerYes — an immediate loading bridge on the same day, with normal function after placement. They return after 6 months. Two visits total.
X10What can a full-mouth All-on-4/6 patient eat after the first visit?
AnswerSoft foods — they have a same-day temporary bridge/crown (immediate loading). They return after 6 months for the final prosthesis.
X11Give a correct online greeting to a new international customer.
Say"Good day Sir, thank you for contacting us. My name is XXX, and I'm a treatment consultant at Huangshan Dental Hospital. Could you please let me know about your major dental concerns?"Rules: concise, clear, easy to understand, courteous — and always greet the customer first.
X12What are the first three questions on the Initial Consultation Record Form?
Answer1. What is the current condition of the teeth in your mouth? 2. What problem do you most want to solve? 3. How is your current physical condition?Q3 is the branch point: healthy → continue; not healthy → contraindications, cannot be treated.
X13What is the last question on the consultation form, and what does each answer trigger?
Answer"Would you mind if we help you make an appointment for a video consultation with a dentist?" — Yes → book the appointment. No → find out the reason.
X14What message do you send after sharing the photo guide?
Say"To provide a more accurate evaluation of your teeth, could you please send us the five photos shown above? This will help our dentist make a careful evaluation and prepare a personalized treatment plan tailored to your dental condition."
X15When should you fill in an overseas patient information file?
AnswerOnly after you receive the treatment plan from the dentist. Photos should only be uploaded once the patient has confirmed they're coming to China and has created an appointment — meaning they've already sent flight ticket information.
X16Name three things a consultant should never do when discussing products.
AnswerNever say one brand is better than another · never push the client toward a specific product · never exaggerate benefits or use irrelevant keywords (and don't rely on AI-generated claims). Also: avoid heavy technical language unless the client asks.
X17What should you ALWAYS include when introducing any implant or veneer product?
AnswerThe country of origin and the price — the manual repeats "always quote the price" for every single product script.
X18Match the technology to its company: Roxolid · TiUnite · SLActive · BLT · Double-lead thread · Conical connection.
AnswerStraumann: Roxolid (material), SLActive (surface), BLT (design) — plus a conical connection. Nobel Biocare: TiUnite (surface), conical connection on NobelReplace CC, double-lead thread on NobelActive, platform shifting.Trap: conical connection belongs to both.
X19Match brand to country: Straumann · Nobel Biocare · MegaGen · Upcera · Ivoclar · VITA · Wieland.
AnswerStraumann — Switzerland · Nobel Biocare — Sweden · MegaGen — South Korea · Upcera — China · Ivoclar — Switzerland · VITA — Germany · Wieland — Germany.
X20Match founding year to company: 1871 · 1923 · 1924 · 1954 · 1981 · 2001 · 2002.
Answer1871 — Wieland · 1923 — Ivoclar · 1924 — VITA Zahnfabrik · 1954 — Straumann · 1981 — Nobel Biocare · 2001 — Upcera · 2002 — MegaGen.
X21Match product-launch year to product: 1997 · 1998 · 2005 · 2008 · 2009 · 2010 · 2015.
Answer1997 — NobelReplace, world's first tapered implant · 1998 — All-on-4® concept · 2005 — IPS e.max · 2008 — NobelActive · 2009 — Roxolid · 2010 — Zenostar product line · 2015 — Straumann's first tapered implant.
X22A patient asks for our social media so they can check us out. What do you offer?
AnswerOur Facebook, Instagram and TikTok pages for Huangshan Dental / Huangshan International Dental Hospital. Customers often request these to learn more about the company.
